chunks: If it had been a nearby gain and an easy journey, they would surely have followed you; but the journey was hard and long for them. And they will swear by God, 'If we had been able, we would have gone out with you,' ruining themselves, and God knows that they are liars.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Hypocrites not join the Prophet in the expedition of Tabuk?
ai.summary: In the context of the Expedition of Tabuk, this verse exposes the psychological mechanism of the Munafiqun, who used the physical hardship of a distant journey as a pretext to avoid jihad while maintaining a facade of loyalty. Shia scholarship emphasizes that their subsequent oaths were not merely lies but a deliberate self-deception that led to their spiritual ruin, illustrating the gap between outward profession and inward conviction. This narrative serves as a timeless warning against using worldly convenience as an excuse for neglecting religious duty.
